en: The Philippines consists of exactly 7,641 islands, which is 1,011 more than the previously recorded 7,107 islands.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River in Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an 8.2-kilometer underground river, which is one of the longest navigable underground rivers worldwide.
The Philippine tarsier is one of the world's smallest primates, measuring only 85 to 160 millimeters in total body length.
The Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones annually, with the typhoon season typically peaking between August and October.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao stretch across 10,360 square kilometers, reaching elevations of up to 1,500 meters above sea level.
The Galathea Depth in the Philippine Trench is the deepest point in the country, plunging 10,540 meters below sea level.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, covering 14,649.7 square kilometers across 1,780 islands.
The Philippines has over 300 active and potentially active volcanoes, with 24 strictly classified as active by the national volcano observatory.
The Sierra Madre mountain range is the longest in the Philippines, stretching approximately 540 kilometers along the eastern coast of Luzon.
